why: The confirming sweep was stopped on the user's instruction after the gate then running had finished -- not concurrently with it and not by force. Completing the full set is deferred to b11.8. The sweep before this one had already done the work a sweep is for: it caught two real violations the fast set cannot reach, and both were repaired and re-verified green by running the affected gates on their own.

prior_sweep_findings.assertion: 09 / 09d no CJK characters in new or added code
prior_sweep_findings.violation: Three lines of code this batch added carried CJK: two docstrings illustrating the annotated name shape with a real example, and one gate stub holding the character as a literal.
prior_sweep_findings.repair: The illustrations are rewritten in English and the literal is an escape with a gloss. Re-verified by running the gate's own scanner over its own globs: zero offenders. Both gates then exited 0, in this run as well.

prior_sweep_findings.assertion: 08e neither chain module imports from the translation pipeline
prior_sweep_findings.violation: chain_backfill imported the line-head punctuation class from the typesetting stage, breaking the purity the module's own docstring states.
prior_sweep_findings.repair: The class is declared in the configuration the module already reads, and gate 02h pins it byte-equal to the stage's constant -- a stronger guard than the import, since an import cannot be checked for content. spec_check_b5 then passed 62/62 standalone.

interrupted_mid_gate_note: spec_check_b2_1.py had already begun when the signal was sent: run_all moves to the next gate the moment one returns, and the watcher saw b2's end line late because the sweep's output is buffered. So b2_1 ran about five minutes and was cut off. The instruction was not to force kill the gate then running, and b2 -- the gate running when the instruction was given -- did finish; b2_1 is the one the gap admitted. Its artifact cache may be half built, so b11.8 should treat b2_1 as unrun rather than resumed.
